label: lem-cauchy-mean-value-quotient-form
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: The lemma assumes `a<b`, so the interval is non‑degenerate and Rolle/Cauchy apply. Division by `g(b)-g(a)` is safe because `g(b)=g(a)` would, via Rolle (applicable since `g` is continuous on `[a,b]` and differentiable on `(a,b)`), contradict `g'(x)≠0`. Division by `g'(c)` is safe because the `c` supplied by Cauchy is in `(a,b)` where `g'` is everywhere nonzero. No counterexample can exist: the product identity from Cauchy combined with the non‑vanishing conditions yields exactly the required quotient. All boundary cases (empty domain, one‑point interval, endpoint choice) are either excluded or properly discharged.

SOURCES: Inspected the exact current text of every cited dependency (`thm-cauchy-mean-value`, `thm-rolle`, `def-derivative`, `def-one-sided-limits`). `thm-cauchy-mean-value` provides the product identity `(f(b)-f(a))g'(c) = (g(b)-g(a))f'(c)` under exactly the continuity/differentiability hypotheses used. `thm-rolle` gives `g'(d)=0` when `g(a)=g(b)`, matching step 1.1. `def-derivative` defines differentiability on `(a,b)` consistently with the statement. `def-one-sided-limits` is not directly invoked but introduces no conflicting convention.

CHECKED: Title, public claim, every numbered step (1.1, 1.2, 2.1), and the absence of Remarks have been verified. No fatal defect found.
